item.title: ‘Crisis Actor’ Appears Deceptively Simple
item.description: True to its deceptively simple nature, Lily Platt's Crisis Actor is a bold and captivating reflection on addiction, albeit of a different kind.

item.title: Alice Costelloe Confronts the Past with Elegant Art Pop
item.description: Alice Costelloe's debut album is refined, elegant art pop, in which her crystalline voice floats over a rich palette of electronic instrumentation with grace.

item.title: Folk Alliance International Offered Comfort in Troubled Times
item.description: January's Folk Alliance International festival served as a place to restore and recharge for folk music lovers, offering solace and inspiration.

item.title: Some Criticism About Criticism
item.description: ​Criticism done well is not antithetical to compassion; the two are closely interlinked as an act of kindness that prevents delusion and leading others astray.

item.title: It’s Funny How Complicated Coexistence Can Be
item.description: Activist-cum-stand-up comedian Noam Shuster-Eliassi documentary Coexistence, My Ass! makes it painfully clear how complicatedly funny/not-funny coexistence can be.

item.title: Cast Follow the Beatles Too Slavishly on ‘Yeah Yeah Yeah’
item.description: Judging by Yeah Yeah Yeah, it seems Cast's vinyl collection consists solely of Rubber Soul, Abbey Road, and The White Album.

item.title: Scorsese’s World Cinema Project #5 Carries Serenity and Chaos
item.description: All the films in Martin Scorsese's World Cinema Project No. 5 showcase filmmakers whose output deserves restoration, but Kummatty offers the most direct and unapologetic sensual pleasures.

item.title: Lucinda Williams Tries to Right What’s Wrong with the World
item.description: The ten tracks on Lucinda Williams' World Gone Wrong are heavy. This ain't no party record. There's too much pain going around in the world.

item.title: Joyce Manor Talk Bars and Candy Bars
item.description: Pop-punk's Joyce Manor have a new album that's a fresh take on their patented sound. "Bands in our scene can have songs from a decade ago blow up on TikTok."

item.title: ElectroMatters: Best Electronic Music of January 2026
item.description: From rough 'n' ready techno to subtle drone, atmospheric footwork to striking synthpop, these are the best electronic records from the past month.
